messages:
Dana H: We need a compact benchmark narrative for the launch landing + two email variants. Focus: how latency affects UX and how serving choices affect cost. Want this nailed by tomorrow so design can mock.
Samir K: Agreed. Audience is infra PMs and platform leads. Their questions: will my app be responsive at scale? how much will this add to my bill?
Priya R: Proposed slide flow for the landing header: 1) One-liner value prop, 2) two-panel visual: left = latency impact (user wait vs conversions), right = unit cost comparison by deployment, 3) quick callouts + CTA.
Theo L: For visuals: latency panel should be a tiny simulated funnel: 0-100ms -> baseline conversions, 100-300ms -> drop-off, 300ms+ -> heavy drop. Use a simple stepped curve and a label: "<200ms = interactive".
Samir K: Cost panel: stacked bars for three scenarios (hosted default, dedicated w/quant, private on prem) showing $/1M tokens and a note for batching efficiency. Add a small table under each bar with assumed throughput and quant level.
Priya R: Copy candidates for header (short): A) "Keep users fast. Cut inference cost." B) "Make inference predictable: latency SLAs, lower unit cost." Which is punchier?
Dana H: I like A for social + hero. B is better for the webinar signup. We'll A/B test.
DesignBot: color palette suggestion: hero accent = #0B66FF (primary), dedicated = #16A34A (green), private = #7C3AED (purple). Also suggest iconography: stopwatch, dollar stack, routing arrows.
Samir K: Metrics to show on the page (we'll call them "typical observed ranges"):
- chat: hosted p95 160-240ms, dedicated p95 40-70ms, cost per 1k tokens hosted $0.035, dedicated $0.007 (w/quant).
- completions (long): hosted p95 350-600ms, dedicated p95 120-220ms, cost per 1k tokens hosted $0.06, dedicated $0.012.
- embeddings: hosted p95 180-300ms, dedicated p95 50-110ms, cost per 1k tokens hosted $0.018, dedicated $0.004.
Priya R: Good ranges. We'll avoid exact claims—use "typical ranges observed in our tests" language and a link to the methods doc.
Theo L: Chart specs (for analytics team):
- Scatter: x=p95 ms (log scale?), y=$/1k tokens, point size=throughput, hue=deployment. Tooltip: workload, model, quant setting, tokens/sec.
- Bar: normalized $ per 1k tokens across quant settings (FP16, int8, int4) with error bars.
- Mini-flow: routing decision tree: low latency -> hosted, high QPS -> dedicated, regulated -> private.
Dana H: For email copy, keep subject lines short. Two variants: V1: "Benchmark: 5x cost wins without latency tradeoffs" V2: "How teams keep latency <200ms and cut inference spend". Body will link to full writeup + sign-up.
Samir K: Lead capture: two-step form. Step 1 minimal: name, email, company, single checkbox for interest (trial / dedicated / private). Step 2 (optional) ask throughput, latency requirement, and compliance needs. That helps sales triage.
DesignBot: place a single prominent CTA: "See the benchmarks" and a secondary smaller "Request dedicated trial".
Priya R: Also add a short FAQ snippet under charts: "How did we measure cost?" "What models were used?" "Can I run my own tests?" linking to a repo.
Dana H: Action list: Samir to export cleaned numeric ranges + CSV by EOD; Theo to sketch chart templates and layout; Priya to draft hero copy + email variants; DesignBot to mock hero and chart styles tomorrow morning.
Samir K: CSV I'll drop will look like: 
```
workload,deploy,p95_ms_low,p95_ms_high,cost_per_1k_low,cost_per_1k_high,throughput_low,throughput_high,quant
chat,hosted,160,240,0.028,0.042,8,18,fp16
chat,dedicated,40,70,0.006,0.009,40,60,int8
completions,hosted,350,600,0.05,0.07,2,6,fp16
completions,dedicated,120,220,0.01,0.014,12,28,int8
embeddings,hosted,180,300,0.015,0.02,60,140,fp16
embeddings,dedicated,50,110,0.003,0.005,240,480,int8
```
Priya R: We'll include a short blurb: "Methods: measurements taken across representative workloads on common open models; dedicated numbers use reserved GPU pools and quantized kernels. See full methods for hardware and prompt shapes."
Dana H: OK everyone — let's aim to finalize copy + CSV by tomorrow 11:00 PT. If the numbers shift we can mark as "preliminary". Thanks! :sparkles:
